s: A company runs hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS account. AWS occasionally schedules instance retirements and maintenance because of underlying host issues, and the team often misses the emails. The company wants the operations channel to be notified automatically, and wants an approved runbook to stop and start the affected instance automatically (a stop and start moves it to healthy hardware). Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
o: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches AWS Health events for scheduled EC2 changes. Send the events to an Amazon SNS topic for the operations channel and as a target that starts an approved AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to stop and start the instance.
Create a CloudWatch alarm on the StatusCheckFailed_System metric for each instance with the EC2 recover action.
Review the AWS Trusted Advisor checks each morning and stop and start any instance that is flagged.
Write an AWS Lambda function that calls the AWS Health API every 5 minutes, parses new events, and sends an email to the operations team.

w.y: AWS Health publishes account-specific events, including scheduled changes such as instance retirement, to Amazon EventBridge at no charge. An EventBridge rule can notify people (SNS, chat) and start automation (Systems Manager Automation, Lambda) with no polling (task 3.1: alerting and automatic remediation).

o.A: Correct. Event-driven notification and remediation with managed services.
o.B: The recover action reacts after a system status check has already failed. It does nothing about a scheduled retirement notice before the event.
o.C: Manual and slow; Trusted Advisor is not the source of scheduled maintenance notices.
o.D: Polling is custom code to maintain, and the AWS Health API needs a Business Support+, Enterprise Support or Unified Operations plan (or a legacy Business, Enterprise On-Ramp or Enterprise plan). EventBridge delivery needs no support plan.

s: Monitoring AWS Health events with Amazon EventBridge
